title: Exploring Psidium guajava L. Leaf Fractions as a Sustainable Source of Antiviral Compounds for the Inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 Spike–ACE2 Interaction (Wuhan and Omicron) and 3CLpro Activity
content: The leaves of Psidium guajava L. (guava) are an underutilized resource containing diverse bioactive metabolites. The present study evaluated the inhibitory potential of P. guajava leaf fractions against two SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets: the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan and Omicron BA.1 variants, and 3CLpro enzymatic activity. A methanolic extract was fractionated by vacuum liquid chromatography, and fraction F14 was then separated into subfractions F14A–F14D through the use of Sephadex LH-20. The activity was evaluated using colorimetric Spike RBD–ACE2 binding assays and a fluorometric 3CLpro assay. F14 and its subfractions inhibited the Spike RBD–ACE2 interaction of the Wuhan variant, whereas against Omicron BA.1, all fractions showed IC₅₀ values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14, F14C, and F14D also inhibited 3CLpro, with IC₅₀ values <1.25 mg mL−1. F14D demonstrated the most consistent inhibitory profile across all the three targets and was selected for further characterization by LC–HRMS. The three major constituents were tentatively assigned as a myricetin hexoside, a quercetin hexoside, and a quercetin pentoside. Overall, the results of this study suggest that F14D contains bioactive constituents with potential inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2 molecular targets, although further studies are required to determine their antiviral activity.
